claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The starting material has residual stresses and a fine grain size typical of additive manufacturing.
Exposure near 900°C in an oxidizing atmosphere promotes grain-boundary oxide-scale growth.
The grain-boundary oxide scale formed under oxidizing conditions is enriched in Ti and Cr.
The oxidizing atmosphere produces a continuous, thicker, and more porous grain-boundary oxide scale than reducing conditions.
Ti and Cr oxidize at different rates at elevated temperature.
The Ti-/Cr-rich grain-boundary oxide is brittle.
Brittle grain-boundary oxides localize stress and act as crack-initiation sites.
Crack initiation at oxidized grain boundaries produces intergranular embrittlement and can culminate in catastrophic failure.
Oxidizing exposure will cause earlier intergranular cracking and mechanical failure than reducing exposure.
Exposure to 5% H2 in Ar suppresses significant grain-boundary oxide accumulation.
Suppressing grain-boundary oxidation preserves grain-boundary integrity.
Samples exposed to reducing conditions will have delayed or absent catastrophic failure relative to oxidizing conditions.
Under standard or mixed reactive-gas baseline conditions, oxide growth is moderate and degradation proceeds at a predictable rate.
The proposed mechanism is applicable around 900°C for exposure times up to 100 hours and atmospheres spanning at least 21% O2 in Ar or pure O2 to 5% H2 in Ar.
